correctness.rationale: The source really specifies state-dependent 0→1 and 1→0 switches with independent coins conditional on the selected vertex; it is not unconditional Bernoulli refresh. With unanimity, the imitation step acts as the identity on environments. A centered edge variable has multiplier r=1−p−q when activated. For two distinct edges, averaging r raised to their number of activations gives a=1−2ωs/N for a single edge and b_j=1−4ωs/N+jωs²/N for a pair sharing j endpoints. This gives the exact means and covariances without a moment closure. With fixed N and M the variance slope in W is 2(h−π)²(b_1^t−b_0^t); the sharp wedge extrema are N−2 (path) and binom(N−1,2) (star), uniquely up to isomorphism. For odd t the slope is positive; for even t its sign is that of b_1+b_0=(2N−ωs(8−s))/N. Since ωs(8−s)<12 and the N=5 admissible example reverses, six is sharp. The product Bernoulli law is invariant under every vertex update and all individual flips and holding have positive probability, so it is the limiting law. Independent integer replay `/workspace/branches/replay-edge-variance.js` enumerates full transition paths for stars and paths on 4–6 vertices over two attempts at the witness rates; it returns 4617/5000 and −1389717/12500000 for N=5. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed. The proof is confined to the stated unanimous, homogeneous-start comparison; replay alone is not the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Whether network shape orders transient aggregate fluctuations, and whether that ordering reverses, are well-motivated questions. But here the submitted invariant and the six-vertex answer are direct second-moment and parity corollaries of the already explicit same-model pair spectrum. The bounded rational illustration is useful exposition but is not a separate mathematical contribution. No distinct repaired claim is established.
